findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify `review_plan_start(ticket_id, engine="pipeline", force=True)` for any pipeline run started after a plan-review attestation exists (the redo-on-new-deploy and retry paths), since idempotent reuse does not check the engine.
evidence: Plan: "The same read is repeated after both runs; if the SHA changed in between, the runs are redone on the new deploy."
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:544-547: `if engine == "pipeline" and sign and not force and not retry: reused = reuse.idempotent_reuse(...)`
reuse.py:139-141: reuse is decided only by `claim_gate_check(ticket_id, ...)`; attest_gate.py's claim_gate_check has no engine check (`engine` appears only in plan_review_status enrichment, :247-263)
reuse.py:168,189-190: reused verdict has `coverage = {"llm_ran": False, "idempotent_skip": True}`, `"model": None`
_mcp_llm.py:282-287: review_plan_start accepts `force: bool = False`
findings.finding: The plan assumes running pipeline first avoids idempotent reuse. But reuse checks `claim_gate_check`, which ignores the engine. Whenever the pipeline run happens after the agentic run has signed a still-valid attestation, it returns the reused PASS (`llm_ran=False`, `model=None`) without calling the model. The plan's own redo path ("if the SHA changed in between, the runs are redone on the new deploy") does exactly that, and it does not use `force=True`. The redone pipeline run would then fail the completion rule.
findings.location: Approach → Preconditions (SHA re-read / redo) and Runs ("Pipeline goes first because …")
scenarios: After both runs the deployed SHA has moved. The operator redoes pipeline, then agentic, on the new deploy. The material is unchanged and the agentic attestation is still certified, so the pipeline redo returns runner=reused with llm_ran=false. The completion rule fails and the ticket is escalated for no real cause.
findings.suggested_fix: In Runs, add: "Any redone or retried pipeline run passes `force=True`: idempotent reuse is decided by claim_gate_check, which accepts an agentic attestation, so an unforced pipeline run after a valid signature returns the reused PASS (llm_ran=false)."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that any redo or repeat of the pipeline run, once a plan-review attestation exists, calls `review_plan_start(ticket_id, engine="pipeline", force=True)` so that idempotent reuse is bypassed and the model is actually called.
evidence: Plan: 'if the SHA changed in between, the runs are redone on the new deploy.'
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:544 — `if engine == "pipeline" and sign and not force and not retry: reused = reuse.idempotent_reuse(...)`
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:120-199 — reuse is decided only by claim_gate_check (no engine check) and returns coverage {llm_ran: False, idempotent_skip: True}
src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:282-288 — review_plan_start takes `force: bool = False`; its docstring says 'force=True creates a fresh one'
findings.finding: The 'runs are redone on the new deploy' step (and any second pipeline run) will return idempotent reuse, not a fresh review. After the first pair of runs, the ticket holds a valid plan-review attestation. reuse.idempotent_reuse only checks claim_gate_check, which does not look at engine, so a repeated pipeline review_plan_start without force returns the stored PASS with coverage.llm_ran=False. That redo can never meet the completion rule.
findings.location: Approach → Preconditions (SHA re-read / 'the runs are redone on the new deploy') and Runs step 1
scenarios: A deploy lands between the pipeline and agentic runs. The redo calls review_plan_start(engine="pipeline") while the attestation from the first run is still valid. gate_status shows passed with verdict PASS, but llm_ran=false, so the completion rule is never met on the new deploy.
findings.suggested_fix: In the SHA-recheck bullet, add: 'Redone runs pass `force=True` to `review_plan_start`. Without it, the existing attestation makes the pipeline engine return idempotent reuse (llm_ran=false).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Call `review_plan_start(..., force=True)` for every redone or retried run (at least the pipeline ones), and record `findings.decided_by_run`, which must be true, so a reused verdict can't count.
evidence: Plan: 'if the SHA changed in between, the runs are redone on the new deploy.'

findings.finding: Redone or retried pipeline runs can't meet the completion rule as written. The plan redoes both runs when the deployed SHA changes, and retries failed runs once, but never passes `force=True`. By then the agentic run's attestation is usually current. idempotent_reuse checks validity through claim_gate_check, which does not care which engine signed, so a non-forced pipeline run returns the reused PASS with `coverage.llm_ran=False` and `runner: 'reused'`. If the reviewed code drifted, it takes the drift_refresh path instead of a full review. Either way `llm_ran` is not true.
findings.location: Approach → Preconditions ('the runs are redone on the new deploy') and Completion rule ('retried once')
scenarios: The deployed SHA changes between run 1 and run 2. The pipeline redo returns the reused PASS from the agentic attestation, llm_ran=false, and the run can never count.
The pipeline run is retried after the agentic attestation exists and is short-circuited the same way.
findings.suggested_fix: In Runs, add: 'A redo after a SHA change, and any retry, calls review_plan_start with force=True; a run counts only if gate_status findings.decided_by_run is true and coverage.idempotent_skip is absent.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Say how a redo or retry gets past attestation reuse: pass `force=True` to `review_plan_start` for every redo and retry, and require `llm_ran=true` on the redone runs.
evidence: Plan: "The same read is repeated after both runs; if the SHA changed in between, the runs are redone on the new deploy."
Plan: "a valid signed attestation makes a later pipeline run return the idempotent-reuse result without calling the model"
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:120-199: reuse fires whenever claim_gate_check is ok, does not check which engine signed, and sets coverage.llm_ran=False
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:196: 'pass --force to re-run'; src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:285-288: review_plan_start accepts `force`
findings.finding: Two fallbacks do not account for idempotent reuse. Redoing both runs on a new deploy (SHA changed) starts the pipeline run with no `force=True`. By then the ticket holds a current attestation signed by the agentic run, so `idempotent_reuse` returns a reused PASS with `llm_ran=false`. The redone pipeline run can then never meet the completion rule. The same applies to any pipeline retry after an attestation already exists.
findings.location: Approach → Preconditions ("if the SHA changed in between, the runs are redone on the new deploy") and Completion rule (retry once)
scenarios: A deploy lands between run 1 and the second SHA read. The redo's pipeline run is answered from the agentic attestation without calling the model.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: "Redos (after a deploy SHA change) and retries call `review_plan_start(ticket_id, engine=..., force=True)` so idempotent/verdict reuse is bypassed; a run whose gate_status shows `decided_by_run == false` does not count."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how a redo or retry of the pipeline run avoids idempotent reuse (e.g. a trivial content edit that changes the plan hash), and that both engines are re-run in pipeline-then-agentic order.
evidence: "if the SHA changed in between, the runs are redone on the new deploy"
"a valid signed attestation makes a later pipeline run return the idempotent-reuse result without calling the model"
findings.finding: Redoing the runs after a SHA change, or retrying a failed agentic run, can make the redone pipeline run hit idempotent reuse. The plan itself says a valid signed attestation makes a later pipeline run reuse the result without calling the model. The redo would then give `coverage.llm_ran` false and fail the completion rule. The plan gives no way to invalidate the existing attestation before the redo.
findings.location: Approach — Preconditions (SHA re-read) vs Runs ordering rationale
scenarios: The deploy changes mid-verification; a pipeline redo on the new SHA returns reuse with llm_ran=false, so the run can never count.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'Before any redo, make a no-op-semantic edit to the target description (e.g. append a dated verification note) so the existing attestation no longer matches, then re-run pipeline then agentic.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how a redo on a new deploy defeats pipeline attestation reuse (e.g., a no-op plan edit that changes the plan hash, or revoking the prior attestation) so the redone pipeline run actually calls the model.
evidence: 'if the SHA changed in between, the runs are redone on the new deploy'
'a valid signed attestation makes a later pipeline run return the idempotent-reuse result without calling the model'
Completion rule requires 'coverage.llm_ran is true'
findings.finding: The redo rule for a deploy change will make the pipeline rerun fail the completion rule. The plan says that if the deployed SHA changed between reads, 'the runs are redone on the new deploy'. However, the pipeline run on the old deploy (or the later agentic run) will already have signed a valid attestation on an unchanged plan. The plan itself notes that a valid signed attestation makes a later pipeline run return the idempotent-reuse result without calling the model. The redone pipeline run would therefore have llm_ran=false and could never satisfy the completion rule.
findings.location: Approach > Preconditions: 'if the SHA changed in between, the runs are redone on the new deploy'
scenarios: The deploy lands mid-procedure. Both runs PASS and sign on the old SHA. The redo of the pipeline run hits reuse, records llm_ran=false, and the ticket can never close without escalation.
findings.suggested_fix: Before redoing on a new SHA, make a recorded, content-neutral change to the target plan that changes its hash (or explicitly invalidate the existing plan-review attestation). Then rerun pipeline first, then agentic, and record that this was done.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a BLOCK branch to the completion rule: record the blocking findings, revise the target plan, re-run the local pre-checks, then redo BOTH production runs in order (pipeline, then agentic) with force=True.
evidence: Plan: "A failed or degraded run (`gate_status` failed, INDETERMINATE, `llm_unavailable`) is recorded with its error and `resolution_class`. It is retried once…"
src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:164-173: a BLOCK is gate_status 'passed' carrying verdict BLOCK, not 'failed'
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:202-246: an unchanged plan with a stored pipeline BLOCK replays that BLOCK (llm_ran=False)
Plan: pre-checks run on 'the worktree CLI (Anthropic API config)'; production uses 'its Bedrock credentials'
findings.finding: Nothing says what to do if a production run completes with a BLOCK verdict (gate_status `passed`, verdict BLOCK, llm_ran true). That outcome is neither in the completion rule nor in the failed-or-degraded list (gate failed / INDETERMINATE / llm_unavailable). The production server uses Bedrock models, while the pre-check used the Anthropic API, so a BLOCK after a local PASS is realistic. A plain retry does not help: `verdict_reuse` returns the stored pipeline BLOCK without calling the model. Revising the plan changes the material fingerprint, which invalidates any attestation already signed, so the order of reruns also needs a rule.
findings.location: Approach → Completion rule
scenarios: The pipeline run BLOCKs in production even though both local pre-checks passed.
The pipeline run PASSes and signs, then the agentic run BLOCKs. Revising the plan invalidates the pipeline attestation already recorded.
findings.suggested_fix: Completion rule: "A run that completes with verdict BLOCK is recorded with its blocking findings; the target plan is revised, re-pre-checked locally under both engines, and both production runs are redone pipeline-then-agentic (force=True), since the revision invalidates any earlier attestation."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default for a substantive production FAIL (e.g. revise the target, then re-run BOTH engines pipeline-then-agentic; this counts as the one retry).
evidence: "pre-checked ... on the worktree CLI (Anthropic API config)"
"A failed or degraded run (`gate_status` failed, INDETERMINATE, `llm_unavailable`) ... is retried once after the cause is checked"
findings.finding: The plan does not define what to do when production returns a substantive FAIL verdict rather than a degradation. The local PASS was obtained under a different config (Anthropic API vs production Bedrock), so a production FAIL is possible. 'Retried once after the cause is checked' does not say whether the plan may be revised before the retry. Revising after a pipeline PASS would also leave the two runs reviewing different plan content.
findings.location: Approach — Completion rule; Target
scenarios: The agentic engine on Bedrock returns FAIL with findings; the executor cannot tell whether to revise the plan, re-run unchanged, or escalate.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish a substantive FAIL verdict from infrastructure degradation: if the target plan is revised, require rerunning both engines (pipeline first) on the new plan version and recording both.
evidence: 'pre-checked with `rebar review-plan --no-sign --source local` under each engine on the worktree CLI (Anthropic API config)'
'A failed or degraded run ... is retried once after the cause is checked'
findings.finding: A genuine FAIL verdict in production is treated like a degraded run ('retried once after the cause is checked'). The plan does not say that fixing the cause means revising the target plan. Such a revision invalidates any attestation already signed by the other engine, so both runs must be redone in pipeline-then-agentic order. The local pre-checks run on the Anthropic API config while production runs on Bedrock, so a production FAIL after a local PASS is realistic.
findings.location: Approach > Completion rule: 'retried once after the cause is checked; if it fails again, this ticket stays open'
scenarios: Pipeline PASSes and signs. Agentic returns FAIL on Bedrock. The operator revises the plan and retries only agentic. The pipeline evidence now refers to a stale plan hash, and no current pipeline attestation exists.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add read-only preconditions: the production MCP server has REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM=1 and is not readonly (REBAR_MCP_READONLY unset or 0, and no [tool.rebar.mcp] readonly), checked through the same SSM read.
evidence: Verified: src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:301-305 — review_plan_start raises unless allow_llm()
Verified: src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:132-139 — `sign=not readonly, emit_sidecar=not readonly`
Absence: the Preconditions list covers the children, the deployed SHA and the Bedrock cap only
findings.finding: The preconditions leave out two server settings the runs depend on. review_plan_start is refused unless the server has REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM=1. Under REBAR_MCP_READONLY the run executes with sign=False and emit_sidecar=False, so a PASS returns unsigned with no REVIEW_RESULT sidecar. The plan checks the deploy SHA and the Bedrock cap, but not these.
findings.location: Approach → Preconditions
scenarios: A readonly production server returns gate_status passed with verdict PASS, but signs no attestation and writes no sidecar. Both runs fail the completion rule and use up the single retry.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Run `git merge-base --is-ancestor <merge-commit> <deployed-sha>` for each of the six children's merge commits, not only 4240326388e.
evidence: "names a commit that contains the engine-choice change 4240326388e (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`)"
Six children listed in the first precondition with no per-child deploy check
findings.finding: The deployed-SHA precondition checks ancestry of only the engine-choice commit 4240326388e. It does not check that the deployed commit contains all six listed engine children. If any child landed after 4240326388e, the live server can pass the precondition while missing part of the engine work.
findings.location: Approach — Preconditions, second bullet
scenarios: [rebar:antifungal-amenable-mite] merges after 4240326388e but before the next deploy; the runs pass on a server without it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Select the production sidecar by excluding `source=local` (and matching engine and timestamp after the job start, or the job id), and fail if none is found.
evidence: "the newest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar for that run (read with the worktree CLI after a fetch)"
"their REVIEW_RESULT sidecars carry `source=local`"
findings.finding: Selecting 'the newest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar for that run' does not say how a sidecar is matched to the run. Local pre-check sidecars (`source=local`) exist for the same ticket. If the fetch has not yet brought down the production sidecar, the newest one is a local pre-check result, and the recorded verdict, model and llm_ran would come from the Anthropic-API pre-check rather than production.
findings.location: Approach — Recorded, second bullet
scenarios: The fetch lags the server write; the executor records the local pre-check verdict as the production evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'the newest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar for that run' with 'the newest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar whose source is not `local`, whose engine matches the run, and whose timestamp is after the job's start'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a poll interval and maximum wait (e.g. 30 min); treat a timeout as a failed run, recorded with the last `gate_status` payload.
evidence: "polled with `gate_status(job_id)` until `passed`/`failed` and `findings.readable`"
findings.finding: Polling with `gate_status(job_id)` 'until passed/failed' has no timeout or maximum wait. There is also no rule for a job that never reaches a terminal state, e.g. a hung Bedrock call or a stuck worker.
findings.location: Approach — Runs, step 1
scenarios: The server-side job hangs and the executor polls indefinitely without classifying it as a failed run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before editing the target, record its original description and file_impact verbatim in a comment on the target, and note in that comment that the plan was written for this verification.
evidence: "its description and `file_impact` are completed"
"edits to the target ticket's own description and `file_impact`"
findings.finding: The plan overwrites the description and file_impact of another open ticket (`mindless-misogynic-nematode`) and leaves a signed attestation on it. It does not preserve the original content or describe how to back the edit out if the eventual owner's intent differs.
findings.location: Approach — Target; Scope
scenarios: The task's owner later finds their stub plan replaced and a plan-review attestation bound to text they did not write.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Also post a comment on this ticket linking the epic evidence comment and listing both job ids and attestation timestamps.
evidence: "recorded in a comment on the epic `pompous-vitriolic-macaw`"
"Evidence lives in a comment on the epic."
findings.finding: The non-codebase evidence is recorded only on the epic. Nothing is recorded on this ticket itself, which the NON-CODEBASE rule expects to carry the concrete attestation.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria; Scope
scenarios: A reviewer closing this ticket finds no evidence or link on it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Claim (or otherwise lock ownership of) mindless-misogynic-nematode for the duration of the edits and production runs, and state that the resulting signed attestation is intentionally left in place.
evidence: 'an open, unclaimed task in this epic'
'The plan is revised until both engines return PASS locally.'
Scope: 'edits to the target ticket's own description and `file_impact`'
findings.finding: The plan revises another ticket's description and file_impact, and leaves a signed attestation on it, without claiming the ticket. Ownership of that shared record is never established. The plan checks that the target is 'open, unclaimed', then edits it over multiple revisions. That is a check-then-act window: another agent could claim and edit the ticket concurrently, which would change the plan hash mid-procedure or overwrite the edits.
findings.location: Approach > Target: '`mindless-misogynic-nematode`, an open, unclaimed task in this epic ... its description and `file_impact` are completed'
scenarios: Another worker claims the target between the local pre-check and the production runs and edits it. The production runs then review a different plan from the one pre-checked, or that worker's edits are clobbered.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step to claim the target ticket before editing it, and to release or hand it back after recording. Note in the epic comment that the attestation on the target is intentional and was produced by this verification.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the expected model ID per engine and add 'recorded model equals the expected model' to the completion rule.
evidence: 'Unit tests cannot show that the deployed server, its signing environment and its Bedrock credentials work with the new engine and models.'
Completion rule lists gate_status, verdict, llm_ran and attestation, but no model check
findings.finding: Nothing in the completion rule checks that the run used the new models. The context says the check must show the deployed server works 'with the new engine and models', and the verdict's `model` and the manifest `model:` line are recorded. But a run counts on gate_status passed + PASS + llm_ran + signed, whatever model it reports. A deploy still routing to an old model would satisfy the acceptance criterion.
findings.location: Approach > Completion rule; Context: 'work with the new engine and models'
scenarios: Production config still points at the previous model ID. Both runs PASS and are recorded as complete, yet the new-model path is never exercised.
findings.suggested_fix: State the expected Bedrock model ID for each engine (from the landed children's config), and require that both the sidecar `model` and the attestation manifest `model:` line match it before a run counts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Stop polling on any terminal gate_status (passed or failed). Wait for findings.readable only on passed runs, and record findings.reason when it stays false.
evidence: Verified: src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:278-283 — a failed run reports readable False with reason 'run-failed'; a run with sidecar_emitted False reports 'sidecar-not-emitted'
findings.finding: The polling rule can loop forever on a failed run. The plan polls gate_status 'until passed/failed and findings.readable'. On a failed or non-emitting run, `findings.readable` stays false (reason 'run-failed' or 'sidecar-not-emitted'), so polling never ends.
findings.location: Approach → Runs step 1 ('polled with gate_status(job_id) until passed/failed and findings.readable')
scenarios: The Bedrock call fails, gate_status reports failed, and the poll waits indefinitely for findings.readable instead of moving to the record-and-retry path.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the poll condition to: 'until status is passed or failed; on passed, keep polling until findings.readable is true or findings.reason is terminal (sidecar-not-emitted / review-result-sidecar-missing), and record that reason.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Require reading `show_ticket(...).attestations["plan-review"]` (and plan_review_status) right after each run reaches a terminal state, before the next run starts, because the map keeps only the latest signature per kind.
evidence: src/rebar/reducer/_processors_identity.py:138-141 (process_signature): "a kindable event sets ``attestations[kind]`` (per-key last-writer-wins, so re-signing one kind replaces only that kind…)"
Both engines sign with kind `plan-review` (manifest.py:36 `_MANIFEST_PREFIX = "plan-review"`).
The plan names a source per field but gives no time to read it, except for plan_review_status ("after the run").
findings.finding: The plan reads each run's attestation fields from `show_ticket(...).attestations["plan-review"]`. That map keeps only the latest signature per kind, so the agentic run's signature replaces the pipeline run's. The plan does not say the pipeline attestation must be read before the agentic run starts. If both are read after both runs, the pipeline's signed `model:` line and attestation evidence can no longer be retrieved there.
findings.location: Approach → Recorded ("each field from a named source … `show_ticket(...).attestations["plan-review"]`")
scenarios: The operator runs pipeline, then agentic, then fills in the one epic comment. show_ticket now shows only the agentic manifest, so the pipeline's `model:` line and its signed status are gone from the named source.
findings.suggested_fix: Under Runs, add: "After step 1 is terminal and before step 2 starts, capture show_ticket(...).attestations[\"plan-review\"].manifest and plan_review_status; the agentic signature replaces this record (last-writer-wins per kind)."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture `show_ticket(...).attestations["plan-review"]` and `plan_review_status` immediately after run 1 reaches terminal state, before starting run 2.
evidence: "attestation signed, the signed `engine:` line and the manifest `model:` line: `show_ticket(...).attestations["plan-review"]`"
"`plan_review_status`'s `verdict` and `engine` after the run"

findings.finding: The plan does not handle a production BLOCK, and its retry rule cannot recover from one. A BLOCK reports gate_status 'passed', so it is not in the plan's 'failed or degraded' list. If a pipeline BLOCK is simply retried, reuse.verdict_reuse returns the stored BLOCK (llm_ran=false) while the plan text is unchanged. Revising the plan to clear a BLOCK changes the material fingerprint. If the BLOCK came from the agentic run, that revision invalidates the pipeline attestation already signed, so both runs must be redone, in pipeline-then-agentic order. The local pre-check uses the Anthropic API config, while production uses Bedrock models, so a local PASS does not guarantee a production PASS. A production BLOCK is therefore a realistic outcome.
findings.location: Approach → Completion rule
scenarios: The production pipeline run BLOCKs on a finding the local Anthropic-config run did not raise. Retrying once without changing the plan replays the same BLOCK.
